Hi Sarah —

Great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. I pulled in Kimberly (sales lead) and Ben (billing/fulfillment engineer) to ensure we cover both procurement and the integration details. Quick answers up front:

- For AWS Marketplace metering, the primary association is the AWS entitlement (Marketplace customer ID) that AWS issues when a customer subscribes through the marketplace. However we can map your internal license_key -> AWS entitlement on our side so usage appears under the Marketplace subscription for invoicing.
- We typically recommend a short-lived sidecar token approach: the customer redeems a marketplace entitlement and we issue a mapping record that links the AWS entitlement_id to your license_key in our entitlement table; this allows your portal to keep using existing keys while AWS metering uses the entitlement_id.
- We provide webhooks for activation, deactivation, and revocation (POSTs to a customer URL). We can send the mapping payload in the activation webhook so your systems get the entitlement_id + license_key pair immediately.

Ben will outline the exact API/field names, and Kimberly can confirm timeline and DocuSign next steps. I can host a call Thu 11/12 10am PT or Fri 11/13 9am PT — which works for your team?

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni

Hi all —

Following up with the technical details Vivek referenced so Acme's engineers can validate against your portal. Summary of recommended implementation:

1) Subscription flow (high level)
- Customer purchases via AWS Marketplace -> AWS creates a Marketplace subscription and entitlement_id.
- Redwood receives a subscription notification from AWS (via SNS/Lambda endpoint) containing the entitlement_id and customer AWS account.
- Redwood calls your sidecar endpoint to exchange the entitlement_id for your internal license_key (we POST {entitlement_id, aws_account, marketplace_product_code}).

2) Mapping table fields (we'll provide a migration script)
- mapping_id (uuid)
- entitlement_id (string)
- customer_id (your internal customer id)
- license_key (string)
- active_from, revoked_at (timestamps)

3) Metering calls
- Redwood will emit MeterUsage calls to AWS with the entitlement_id; your billing reports can reconcile using the mapping table we export daily.

4) Webhooks
- Activation: POST /webhooks/marketplace/activation -> {entitlement_id, license_key, mapped_at}
- Revocation: POST /webhooks/marketplace/revocation -> {entitlement_id, license_key, revoked_at}

Security notes:
- We sign webhooks with HMAC-SHA256. Please provide a webhook TLS endpoint and an HMAC secret exchange mechanism (we can share via your SSO/secret manager or DocuSign protected attachment).
- For the migration period we recommend a reconciliation job that consumes both your usage logs and the Marketplace metering reports to ensure zero gaps.

I'll drop a short Postman collection and a CSV export template before the call.

- Ben

Senior Billing Engineer, Redwood Inference
